task: Review every supplied part, discover the most consequential events from the supplied evidence, cluster related reports, assign the best-fit broad news category dynamically and produce up to 150 processed stories using schema/processed-news.schema.json. The final portfolio must contain at least five well-supported stories in every category. Treat social attention as a discovery signal rather than verification. More than half of the final stories must originate with independent, local or social discovery, using the first source in each story as the discovery source; established outlets may account for no more than half.

items.title: Gruha Lakshmi beneficiaries can't claim ₹2,000 assistance as right: State to Karnataka High Court
items.summary: The Karnataka government on Thursday told the Karnataka High Court that beneficiaries of the Gruha Lakshmi scheme cannot claim the monthly financial assistance of ₹2,000 as a matter of right. A Bench of Justices Anu Sivaraman and KS Bharath Kumar was hearing a public interest litigation (PIL) filed by Bengaluru-based labourers alleging that the State has failed to release ₹5,000 crore towards arrears of two instalments of ₹2,000 each to 1.26 crore women beneficiaries of the scheme. Justice Anu Sivaraman and Justice KS Bharath Kumar The State has contended that the implementation of the welfare scheme is subject to administrative exigencies and the State's financial constraints. In its statement of objections, the State government has argued that the existence of a benevolent welfare scheme does not confer an indefeasible right on beneficiaries to demand financial assistance through judicial intervention. items.title: Delhi court halts police action against Congress MP and JNU professor A Bimol Akoijam
items.summary: A Delhi court on Thursday directed that Delhi Police should not take any coercive action against Congress Member of Parliament (MP) and Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) professor A Bimol Akoijam in connection with the sexual harassment case against him. Several students have levelled allegations of sexual harassment against Akoijam, pursuant to which the Delhi Police registered a first information report (FIR) for offences of sexual harassment under Section 75 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Special Judge Digvinay Singh of the Rouse Avenue Courts said that seven days' notice must be given to Akoijam if his arrest is required. The court noted that Akoijam has clear antecedents and that he has been cooperating in the investigation. It added that the investigation is ongoing and victims' statements have yet to be recorded because the JNU administration has not provided their names and details. Further, Judge Singh said that in case of non-cooperation in the probe, Delhi Police is at liberty to approach the court for necessary directions. items.title: Karnataka High Court initiates suo motu case on violence against lawyers; seeks report from State
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Tuesday initiated a suo motu case to examine the increasing incidents of violence, assaults, threats and murders of advocates across the State and the need to ensure adequate protection to members of the legal fraternity. A Division Bench of Justice DK Singh and Justice H Shanti Bhushan directed the High Court registry to register a case as public interest litigation (PIL) following representations by the Advocates Association, Bengaluru (AAB), and the Karnataka State Bar Council (KSBC), highlighting the recent murders of advocates Sriram V and Manjunath, and the alleged attempt to murder Senior Advocate Venkataramanappa Sannakki. “An attack upon an advocate, particularly one resulting in the loss of life, cannot be viewed as an isolated incident, since it also affects the independence of the Bar and the administration of justice,” the Court said. items.title: Supreme Court says 24-hour arrest deadline begins when person is detained
items.summary: The Supreme Court has ruled that the 24-hour deadline for producing an arrested person before a magistrate begins from the moment their liberty is curtailed, and not from the time the police formally record the arrest. A bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S Chandurkar held that excluding the period of detention before a formal arrest from the 24-hour deadline would violate Article 22(2) of the Constitution. The ruling came in appeals filed by four people challenging the Tripura High Court's rejection of their bail pleas in a case under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act. The four accused were detained on September 29, 2025, at around 2 pm during a search and seizure operation. However, the police formally recorded their arrest only at 11 am the following day. The Supreme Court held that they should have been produced before a magistrate within 24 hours of their detention on September 29. According to a LiveLaw report, the court found that the accused had been kept in custody for around 18 hours without judicial oversight, violating their constitutional rights. items.title: Remarks about Sikhs: Allahabad High Court declines FIR against Rahul Gandhi, says he has right to voice concerns of minority
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court on Thursday rejected a plea seeking the registration of a First Information Report (FIR) against Congress leader Rahul Gandhi in relation to the remarks made by him about religious freedom in India, in relation to the Sikh community [Nageshwar Mishra and another v State of UP and another] Justice Vikram D Chauhan noted that Gandhi had said that there is an atmosphere of insecurity among Sikhs in India. The Court observed that the statement only raised concerns about a community or section of society. Gandhi as an elected representative has the right to raise concerns in respect of a minority community, the bench added. "The respondent no. 2 being an elected representative has a right to raise concerns in respect of section of society. Further, questioning the rights of minorities by elected representative by itself cannot be an offence and the said speech of respondent no. 2 will have protection of freedom of speech and expression under Article 19 of Constitution," the Court said. items.title: Centre supports plea in Supreme Court to deny post-resignation perks to tainted constitutional functionaries
items.summary: The Central government on Thursday told the Supreme Court that the public interest litigation (PIL) seeking to deny post-resignation perks and amenities to constitutional functionaries, including judges, who quit to avoid removal proceedings, appeared to have merit [Pratik Vira v Union of India] . Solicitor General Tushar Mehta , appearing for the Central government, acknowledged before a Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi that the petitioner, one Pratik Vira, appeared to have made out a case. He then undertook to obtain instructions and file a response. The Court, subsequently, allowed an intervention application and directed the Union government to file its counter-affidavit. items.title: Punjab & Haryana High Court asks Centre to examine whether LPU violence warrants NIA probe
items.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has directed the Central government to examine whether the National Investigation Agency (NIA) needs to take over the ongoing Punjab Police probe into the recent violence and arson at Lovely Professional University (LPU) [Ravi Raj v Union of India & Ors] A bench of Chief Justice of Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor passed the order on Wednesday in a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) petition seeking a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into the violence that broke out after false rumours spread about alleged sexual assault of a female student on LPU campus. The Court noted that the police, during the course of the investigation, has found material which prima facie indicates applicability of the offence of cyber terrorism under Section 66F of the Information Technology Act, 2000. Considering that Section 66F is a scheduled offence under the National Investigation Agency Act, the Court directed the State to forward a report with regard to commissioning of the offence in terms of Section 6 of the NIA Act, to the Central government. items.title: Goa SIR: Bombay High Court orders ECI to add back names of 6 voters deleted from electoral rolls
items.summary: In an order of significant political import, the Goa bench of the Bombay High Court on Thursday ordered the Election Commission of India (ECI) to add back names of six voters deleted from the voters' list during the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in the State. After extensive hearings for four days, a division bench of Justices Valmiki Menezes and Amit Jamsandekar pronounced the verdict on Thursday. "We have allowed petition. We have also rejected the prayer to keep this petition pending till Supreme Court decides (SIR's validity). We issue mandamus and direct the officer to include names of petitioners after confirming residence within 10 days," the Court said pronouncing its order. ECI counsel Gaurish Agni sought a stay on the order. However, the Court refused. "No stay. How can we grant stay on including names of voters in the list! You get a stay from Supreme Court," the bench said. Justices Valmiki Menezes and Amit S. items.title: Karnataka High Court allows BJP MLA’s plea to disband additional land committee headed by Congress leader
items.summary: Public office cannot be treated as a consolation prize for a defeated politician, said the Karnataka High Court recently while quashing a notification that set up an additional land regularisation committee in Byndoor headed by a Congress leader who had lost the 2023 Assembly election [ Gururaj Gantihole v State of Karnataka ]. A Division Bench of Justices DK Singh and H Shanthi Bhushan found that the State had constituted the committee, with Congress leader K Gopal Poojary as its Chairman, without recording any opinion on the need for such an additional committee under Section 94-A(2-A) of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964. The Court observed that the committee appeared to have been constituted on the strength of requests by Poojary, made after his Assembly poll defeat. The notification constituting the additional committee had also adopted the team he had proposed, it noted. items.title: Bombay High Court grants relief to Ananya Panday in personality rights suit
items.summary: The Bombay High Court on Thursday granted interim relief to Bollywood actor Ananya Panday in her suit seeking the protection of her personality and privacy rights [ Ananya Panday v. Fankaar Live Experiences Pvt. Ltd. & Ors. ]. The order passed by Justice Madhav Jamdar addresses widespread unauthorised commercial exploitation and digital manipulation of her name and image. The ex-parte order directs various defendants, including e-commerce giants, and social media platforms, to immediately halt the rampant misuse of the actor’s name, image, likeness, voice, and signature. Justice Madhav Jamdar Panday’s plea flagged unauthorised merchandise sales, false representations by talent agencies claiming authority to facilitate her professional bookings, and the unlawful circulation of deepfakes. Furthermore, it raised concerns over AI-enabled chatbots actively impersonating Panday, alongside the dissemination of digitally manipulated, highly offensive, and sexually explicit content across various digital platforms like Meta, X Corp, and Reddit.
